title: Mini-batcher hedging and kernel preemption to reduce embedding tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: p99 embedding latency remains above our SLA during mixed-size bursts: small requests (1-4 vectors) occasionally experience >600ms tails caused by straggler kernels and bursty queue dynamics. Goal: reduce embed endpoint p99 by 30-40% for small-size requests without regressing throughput or increasing median cost by >5%.

Proposed approach (three orthogonal levers):
1) Mini-batcher hedging: introduce a short, low-latency mini-batch window (1-3ms) that opportunistically coalesces tiny requests. If a request would otherwise wait longer than a hedging deadline, issue a hedged dispatch to a fast-path executor (see experiments below) so the request is not blocked by slow coalescing. Hedging policy tunables: delay_ms, max_mini_batch_size, hedged_retry_limit.

2) Kernel preemption & short-run dispatch: add an executor-level preemption hint that prefers scheduling short, low-sequence kernels ahead of long-running kernels when inflight tail risk is detected. Implement a cheap estimator at enqueue-time (expected_tokens) to classify jobs into short/long buckets and allow short jobs to preempt a fraction of GPU slots (soft preemption via slot reservations, not killing).

3) Quantile-aware admission control and fallbacks: use a live q90/q95 estimator per-tenant to throttle coalescing aggressiveness and trigger quantized-fallback kernels for latency-sensitive traffic. This keeps cost-effective batching for bulk loads while protecting small, latency-sensitive requests.

Success metrics:
- p99 for 1-4 vector requests reduced by >=35% in staging heatbench (target: from median 620ms -> <=400ms)
- median token cost delta < +5%
- throughput for large batches (>=256) no more than 5% degradation in steady-state
- no increase in GPU OOM or kernel failures in CI

Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout in runtime-1.20 canary pool -> 10% production traffic -> 50% -> full. During canary keep a mirrored route to baseline model for top-5 tenants to compute regression deltas (quality/cost). Automatic rollback if p99 increases by >5% for any tenant or if kernel failure rate increases by >1e-4.

Artifacts / links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/ENG/mini-batcher-hedging-design
- Profiling dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/embed-hedge/overview
- Experiment notebook and traces: gs://redwood-internal/embeddings/hedge-experiments/trace-2025-02-24.jsonl
- Initial PR (prototype): https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving/pull/1234

Risks & trade-offs:
- Hedging duplicates a small fraction of requests; must control cost and avoid double-charging for users (billing integration required).
- Preemption is soft: misclassification may hurt throughput. Need conservative defaults and telemetry to tune.
- Complexity added to scheduler increases testing surface; ensure unit + integration + GPU e2e tests.

Next steps: finish prototype PR, run 48h heatbench with synthetic small-batch-heavy traffic, iterate on hedging delay and preemption reservation fraction, prepare canary rollout playbook and cost/billing integration.

2025-02-20 - SRE (Liu Wei): Concern: duplicated hedged requests can complicate audit logs and billing. We should add a dedup header and opt-in flag per-tenant. Filed follow-up ticket PM-412 for billing integration.

2025-02-24 - Marco Ruiz: Ran 24h heatbench with mixed workload (10% small requests). Hedging + conservative preemption gives p99 improvement ~36% on staging; throughput loss ~2.1% on large requests. Dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/embed-hedge/compare
2025-02-27 - Design (Eleni Park): UX note: expose hedging toggle and target latency in Console per-route controls; also show hedging hit-rate in per-route dashboard. Added to console backlog: PM-518.
